status: EXPERIMENTAL - R&D only, not used by any published number

settings.pairs: evidence `comparisons` with kind == comparison (legitimate pairs only)
settings.snr_definition: flux / sqrt(sigma_a^2 + sigma_b^2), sigma^2 = 1/sum(ePSF^2/VARIANCE) on native pixels
settings.psf: ePSF of the target zone, averaged over 4x4 sub-pixel phases (and 4x4 on b's grid for b); b's PSF built through the local WCS Jacobian + bilinear interpolation

kernels.gauss: covariance difference of the two PSFs, 7x7
kernels.al: Gaussians x polynomials ((0.5, 4), (1.0, 2), (2.0, 2)), 7x7, unit sum, fitted to the PSF models

settings.zogy: F_r = F_n = 1, S_corr with full VARIANCE maps; colored: b's noise = white (x) mean bilinear kernel
settings.forced_statistic: aperture difference as compare.photometry (direct, gauss, al); S_corr Fourier-interpolated to the position (zogy)
settings.blank_positions: >= 8 px from target, >= 3 px from Gaia stars (RW Aur) and the control star, 5x5 around clean

zogy_assumptions.known_shift_invariant_psf: VIOLATED: FWHM ~1.2-1.5 px, the pixel image depends on sub-pixel phase. Handled by a phase-averaged PSF; the residual mismatch is measured as match_residual.
zogy_assumptions.psf_of_reprojected_epoch: Handled: b's ePSF sampled on b's pixels then bilinearly interpolated through the WCS.
zogy_assumptions.white_noise: VIOLATED: source noise, nebulosity (RW Aur), and interpolation correlation. Handled by full VARIANCE maps in S_corr and, in zogy_colored, an average interpolation kernel; not by sky structure.
zogy_assumptions.flux_scale_known: ASSUMED F_r = F_n = 1 (calibrated MJy/sr); not fitted, 0-1 control stars per cutout.
zogy_assumptions.no_resampling_covariance: VIOLATED by reprojection; only zogy_colored models it, as a cutout average.

recommendation_rule:
(fixed before running) "direct" = direct_aperture, production):
  INTEGRATE a method only if, on both targets, (1) its blank-position null width (MAD)
  is within 0.9-1.1 and its std is no worse than direct, (2) its completeness at S/N 7
  beats direct by >= 5 points at the same threshold or it has fewer false positives
  at equal completeness, (3) it keeps every published claim (8/8 RW Aur pairs >= 5,
  0/27 WISE 0855 pairs >= 5) and (4) it runs in < 1 s per pair. Otherwise DO NOT INTEGRATE.

interpretation: Real pixels, 8 RW Aur and 27 WISE 0855 pairs (the legitimate comparisons). The direct method reproduces every published significance (max difference 1e-14 sigma). Clean field (WISE 0855), 254 blank spots: ZOGY with the interpolation noise model has a calibrated null (MAD 0.97, std 1.8); so does the production aperture difference in its core (MAD 0.96) but with heavy tails (std 3.8); the PSF-weighted direct difference is too wide (MAD 1.18: it ignores the interpolation correlation), AL more so (1.45). SIMULATED point sources at S/N 7, threshold 5 x the measured null width: ZOGY 94%, direct PSF-weighted 75%, production aperture 16% (nominal threshold: 11%; ideal 98%). Most of the gain over production comes from weighting by the PSF instead of a 2 px aperture with an annulus-scatter error; matching the PSFs adds the rest. Structured field with a bright variable (RW Aur): no method has a calibrated null (MAD 1.24-1.55 for the PSF-weighted ones, 0.2-0.4 for aperture sums whose annulus picks up RW Aur). ZOGY's tails are worst within 11 px of RW Aur (std 5.1 vs 1.5 further out): most likely its matched filter spreading RW Aur's real x1.6-2.5 change (S/N ~300) over the small cutout. PSF matching does what it should on a constant star: at the RW Aur control star the PSF-weighted direct difference reaches 17 sigma (PSF mismatch), the AL-matched one 3 sigma. But convolution grows the masks: AL loses the target in 11 of 27 WISE pairs and in 1 of 8 RW Aur pairs. Published claims hold under every method that returns a number: RW Aur >= 5 sigma in every pair, WISE 0855 below 5 sigma in every pair (largest 2.2 with ZOGY). One WISE 0855 pair (2025W46_1A_0090_2|2026W17_1B_0507_3) has a real point source in the later epoch at a blank spot, >= 5 sigma with every method; it is in the pixels, not an artefact of any method, and we have not identified it. By the rule fixed beforehand: DO NOT INTEGRATE any of them. ZOGY (interpolation noise) passes every criterion on WISE 0855 and fails only on RW Aur, so it is the candidate worth a second look for faint targets in clean fields, with a per-field null calibration; it is not a drop-in replacement. Injected sources are SIMULATED; everything else is real pixels.
